criteria.reasoning: The memo opens: "Gerald T. Halvorsen died at home on August 27, 2026." It then confirms the death under DR-7 through the obituary and the probate filing.

The memo says "Recommendation: cancel the solicitation purpose of the September 29 visit", and Action 2 says to "cancel September 29 visit". It notes that staff "may not propose a memorial naming to the family during the bereavement period." The proposal is not presented to the family.

Action 2 says to "close proposal PR-2026-044 as 'Closed — donor deceased'", and Section 1 adds that a closed proposal "is not transferred to a family member" and that a new one requires VP approval after bereavement. Action 9 says to suspend "any 2026 gallery proposal" until 2027-02-23, but it treats any later proposal as a new one needing VP approval. I read that as no gallery proposal during bereavement, not as reviving PR-2026-044.

Action 2 calls to "mark record 10388 deceased with date of death August 27, 2026" and to "remove decedent from all appeals/mailings/e-mails/invitations including Fall Appeal mail file before September 28 printer pull." Both the deceased update and the appeal removal are covered.
The memo states "Date of death August 27, 2026 = 180th day is February 23, 2027" and uses the flag "Bereavement — no solicitation before [February 23, 2027]." That is the required date.

Action 3 says to "Suppress Fall Appeal rows for 10388 and 20417 from the September 28 printer file". Section 5 also bars the Doyle household from appeals before February 23, 2027. Both Margaret's household row and Kristin's row are removed.

Action 9 says to "Suspend Halvorsen Family Foundation October 15 letter of request... until on/after February 23, 2027", and Section 5 calls that letter "a solicitation barred during bereavement." The foundation is flagged in Action 2, and its trustees are listed in Section 2.
The memo states "$200,000 − $130,000 = $70,000 unpaid balance" and lists the five applied payments. It notes the CRM's $80,000 predates the June 2026 payment.

Action 6 refers the balance to "CFO Denise Okafor decides and communicates" and says "Send no reminder and make no payment ask to family or foundation." Section 3 restates that development staff never ask the spouse, children, foundation or personal representative to pay.
The CFO referral includes "Personal Representative Erik T. Halvorsen, and claim deadline December 28, 2026" along with case No. 2026PR000214. Both required items are given correctly.

Action 7 says "Relationship manager Ruth Kaminski notifies → Director of Planned Giving Samuel Achterberg acts", and the "Director alone contacts Personal Representative/attorney Laura Vang." No one else is told to ask about the will.
The bequest is called an "expectancy", and Action 7 says "Do not book as revenue/receivable/campaign credit." Section 4 adds it is not booked until distribution is received.

Action 5 says "Prepare Center condolence letter for signature by President & CEO Laurel Whitfield, co-signed by Board Chair Thomas Brandvold because decedent was a current/former trustee." That is the required signer and co-signer.
Action 8 addresses the three memorial gifts and says to "send next of kin monthly donor name/address list; never share amounts with family." That meets the names-not-amounts requirement.

Every family, estate and gift fact traces to the files: death at home, age, survivors, trustees, probate details and gift amounts. No cause of death or estate value is given. The bequest is reported only as the 2021 letter states it, and the memo says the files do not show "whether the $100,000 bequest remains".
